routing_warnings.description: The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it concerns the hosted review environment rather than web-application behavior.
The client asks where the web and app source code can be accessed, which concerns complete source-code delivery rather than operation of the web application.
The freelancer identifies the frontend source-code location; this is evidence about source-code delivery, not implementation or verification of the web application.
The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it does not establish failure of the Android application.
The client is asking where to find the Flutter application source code, which concerns source-code delivery rather than Android application behavior.
The freelancer identifies the location of the frontend source code but does not claim that an Android build was completed or verified.
The message separately proposes releasing the application on Google Play, which belongs to the store-release Requirement rather than the Android application deliverable.
This message requests Apple App Store release services rather than changing or verifying the iOS application deliverable itself.
The request for access to the full web and app codebase concerns source-code delivery rather than the Flutter technology constraint.
The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it concerns review-environment availability rather than implementation of the backend using NestJS.
The client requests replacement of exposed API endpoints, which belongs to the dedicated exposed-configuration replacement Requirement rather than the NestJS framework constraint.
The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend is not deployed; it does not establish a PostgreSQL-specific failure.
The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it does not provide evidence about use of Prisma ORM.
The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it does not identify or report a state of the Redis service.
This message concerns availability of platform resources and developer access for application distribution, not multi-user product support.
This message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it does not report a multi-user access failure.
This message identifies the location of frontend source code and does not claim implementation of multi-user support.
The message explicitly requires sharing an existing PDF invoice through specified channels; it does not independently introduce or verify PDF generation.
The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it does not address daily automatic backup behavior.
The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it does not concern restoration from a backup.
The message reports that hosted testing is unavailable because the backend has not been deployed; it does not report a failure of email OTP authentication.
The inability to perform hosted testing concerns availability of the hosted review environment rather than delivery of the source code.
The publicly visible repository concerns repository access control rather than completeness of source-code delivery.
The client requests deployment instructions for a server administrator, not general project installation and configuration guidance.
The client explicitly requests a step-by-step deployment document, which belongs to the separate deployment-guide Requirement.
The freelancer commits to sending a deployment document, not a general project setup guide.
The freelancer disputes responsibility for deployment generally in the context of the client's requested server deployment; the message does not specifically identify Docker configuration.
This message specifies the environment for final deployment to the client's server rather than the temporary hosted review environment.
This message reasserts the Docker deployment requirement rather than changing the hosted review environment.
This message requests a temporary live environment for client review rather than deployment to the client's Ubuntu VPS.
This message requests written deployment instructions for a server administrator rather than actual deployment by the freelancer.
This message explicitly concerns the Docker deployment requirement, not execution of a release to the client's Ubuntu VPS.
The publicly visible repository is a concrete repository-access issue with its own narrower Requirement.
The online exposure of the project path concerns repository access control; the API exposure also supports the separate API-configuration remediation Requirement.
The private-repository implementation claim belongs to the narrower repository-access Requirement.
The request to replace exposed API endpoints belongs to the incident-specific configuration-remediation Requirement.
This message requires replacement of exposed API endpoints rather than changing repository access control.
